summary.headline: Bajaj Finserv Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT attributable to owners rose 23% to INR 2,758 crores; General Insurance PAT fell to INR 420 crores on NATCAT and lower capital gains.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income grew 17% to INR 43,416 crores and consolidated PAT grew 25% to INR 5,952 crores, with PAT attributable to owners up 23% to INR 2,758 crores. Bajaj Finance posted AUM growth of 26% and PAT of INR 6,367 crores (+29%), while Bajaj Life's VNB rose 40% to INR 512 crores with rolling 12-month NBM at 20.8%. Bajaj General's combined ratio rose to 104.5% (from 102.3%) on NATCAT claims of INR 75 crores net and lower capital gains. Management flagged distribution-reform consultation paper and Ind AS transition from 1 April 2027 as the key sector watch items.

segments.name: Bajaj General Insurance
segments.commentary: GWP INR 7,056 crores (+10%, vs industry about 12%); health +31% and motor +18%. Underwriting loss INR 115 crores vs INR 92 crores; annualised ROE 16.2%; solvency about 230%.

segments.name: Bajaj Life Insurance
segments.commentary: VNB +40% to INR 512 crores; rolling 12-month NBM 20.8%, above 20% despite GST. Retail protection +51% and group protection +81%; AUM INR 146,322 crores (+11%); solvency 255%.

segments.name: Bajaj Finance and Bajaj Housing Finance
segments.commentary: BFL: NTI +23% to INR 15,974 crores, loan losses to AUF 1.56% (1.88% prior year), CAR 20.3%; board approved INR 11,700 crores QIP and INR 5,800 crores warrants to Bajaj Finserv. BHFL: AUM crossed INR 1.5 lakh crores (+25%), gross NPA 0.29%, CAR 21.2%.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Health
segments.commentary: 5.7 million healthcare transactions in the quarter, but revenue declined YoY due to partnership restructuring after RBI NBFC business-conduct circular. Network: 1,30,000+ doctors, 32,000+ hospitals, 10,000+ lab touchpoints.

segments.name: Bajaj Markets
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 2,535 crores (Q1: INR 2,269 crores; prior-year Q2: INR 1,549 crores); operating revenue INR 120 crores (+45%); 106 unique partners; targeting quarterly breakeven in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Bajaj Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM about INR 35,760 crores (+24%), ranked 26th among mutual funds; equity mix 60%; incremental SIP book +42%, SIP folios +41%. Launched PMS business and first close of real estate AIF.

guidance_outlook: Bajaj Finance expects opex to net total income to improve by 25-40 bps in FY27 on AI-led efficiencies.
Bajaj Life: management sees rolling 12-month NBM of 20.8% as a reasonable baseline but warned against expecting further large margin expansion.
Bajaj Finserv Health cash consumption to be below INR 200 crores this year and lower next year; breakeven targeted in the year after.
Bajaj Finserv Direct expected to break even on quarterly basis this year and full-year next year.
Bajaj AMC needs about INR 300 crores more capital until breakeven, expected around FY2029 at INR 90,000-100,000 crores AUM.
Management expects less than INR 2,000 crores of investment across businesses in the next 18 months, funded from about INR 4,700 crores surplus capital plus dividends.
capex_capacity: Bajaj Life commenced GIFT City operations in October 2026; retail business with IndusInd Bank to start from Q3 FY27, with pickup expected from Q4.
Reinsurance venture in process of filing for IRDAI approvals; about INR 500 crores needed over 2-3 years.
ALTs business requires sponsor capital of about INR 1,100 crores in roughly a year.
Both insurers to transition to Ind AS from 1 April 2027; management expects no deferral.
Bajaj Finance and BHFL capital: BFL CAR 20.3%, BHFL CAR 21.2%.
demand_pricing: Bajaj General health growth driven by tender-driven business, which carries lower expense ratio but higher loss ratio; tender contracts run 2+1 years.
Bajaj Life shifted mix toward protection: retail term mix up about 3.4 pts, agency protection sales +54% YoY; non-par share 19.7% vs 17.1% last year.
Bajaj Life persistency dipped in 13th and 25th month cohorts, linked to a non-par product and weak markets.
Distribution consultation paper on commissions could affect credit-linked GI and credit life; Bajaj Life says impact on credit life to be partly offset by bulk and retail term opportunities.
Bajaj General's motor retention decision is taken annually; management sees no need to change it now.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in General Insurance health loss ratio, and will motor NATCAT lead to lower retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Avais Karmali said health loss ratio rise reflects a higher share of low-expense but higher-loss tender business in NEP mix, expected to ease as tenders run 2+1 years. Motor rise is NATCAT-driven; retention is reviewed annually and no change is planned now. Ramandeep Sahni said the largest 10-year net NATCAT hit was under INR 100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bajaj Life agency growth slow and is the non-par to annuity shift margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarun Chugh said agency growth slowed as the company prioritised protection mix; agency protection sales rose 54% YoY. Vipin Bansal said non-par was about 13% and annuity about 10% of mix in the latest quarter, versus 18% and 5% a year earlier, and declined to compare margins across the two.

qa_highlights.question: How will the distribution commission proposals affect GI health, credit and motor TP lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Tapan Singhel argued GI mis-selling is negligible and bank partnerships serve a purpose, and declined to quantify credit-attachment share. Sreenivasan said motor TP is a government-tariff product and must be assessed alongside final guidelines; about 80% of health and protection lives are group.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook and is 20.8% the new normal for Bajaj Life?
qa_highlights.answer: Vipin Bansal said 20.8% rolling 12-month NBM is a reasonable baseline with aspiration to expand. Tarun Chugh cautioned that the 4.6 pt expansion in the quarter will not sustain. Sreenivasan said VNB growth of 53% for the half year is the key metric.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Bajaj Life cost base meet commission cuts under the consultation paper?
qa_highlights.answer: Vipin Bansal said the GWP expense ratio already fell about 1% YoY; the proposed commissions, excluding GST and stamp duty, would remove a further roughly 8%, so about 9% in total versus FY2026, with compliance due by end-FY2029.

qa_highlights.question: How will the group fund investments across emerging businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramandeep Sahni said less than INR 2,000 crores is needed over 18 months across Health, Direct, AMC, reinsurance and ALTs. Surplus capital of about INR 4,700 crores plus dividends should cover this, with a possible one-time Ind AS migration surplus release as upside.

risks_watch: Distribution reform consultation paper: commission cuts could hit GI motor/credit-linked, health and Bajaj Life credit life lines; draft regulations pending.
Bajaj General combined ratio at 104.5%; monitor health loss ratio normalisation as tender mix moves and Q2 NATCAT effects.
Bajaj Life persistency dips in 13th and 25th month cohorts; agency growth slowed.
Bajaj Finserv Health revenue declined YoY due to partnership restructuring; H2 outlook uncertain.
Ind AS transition for insurers from 1 April 2027, with management expecting no deferral.
Bajaj Finance QIP of INR 11,700 crores and INR 5,800 crores warrants subject to shareholder approval.
summary.management_tone: Confident on lending, Life VNB and AMC growth, but cautious on distribution reforms and health claims. Management repeatedly declined to quantify commission or margin impact, calling the consultation paper premature, and on Life margins cautioned against raising expectations.

adds.what: Bajaj Life GIFT City operations (commenced Oct 2026); retail business with IndusInd Bank starting Q3 FY27
Reinsurance venture (about INR 500 crore needed over 2-3 years; awaiting IRDAI approvals)

growth.why: Total income grew 17% and consolidated PAT 25% in Q2; guidance is mostly cost and efficiency-led (Bajaj Finance opex/NTI improvement of 25-40 bps in FY27 on AI efficiencies), with Bajaj Markets targeting Q4 FY27 quarterly breakeven and Bajaj Life VNB up 40%, backed by partial specifics but no explicit capacity or order-book figures for revenue growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Bajaj Finance expects opex/NTI to improve 25-40 bps in FY27 on AI efficiencies, but Bajaj Life management warned the 4.6 pt NBM expansion will not sustain and GI combined ratio rose to 104.5% from 102.3%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bajaj Life GIFT City operations commenced Oct 2026 and the IndusInd Bank retail business starts Q3 FY27 with pickup from Q4; reinsurance venture needs about INR 500 crores over 2-3 years pending IRDAI approval.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Bajaj Finance AUM grew 26% to about INR 584,000 crores, BHFL AUM crossed INR 1.5 lakh crores (+25%), and Bajaj AMC AUM rose 24% to about INR 35,760 crores; Bajaj General GWP grew only 10% vs industry about 12%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation metric was disclosed; the main new commitments are about INR 500 crores for reinsurance and about INR 1,100 crores of ALTs sponsor capital in roughly a year, against about INR 4,700 crores surplus capital and less than INR 2,000 crores of 18-month investment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Bajaj Markets is on track for quarterly breakeven in Q4 FY27 (disbursements INR 2,535 crores vs INR 2,269 crores in Q1), and consolidated PAT grew 25% to INR 5,952 crores, but no revenue or volume guidance was raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The distribution consultation paper could cut commissions by about 8% more for Bajaj Life (about 9% total vs FY2026) and hit GI credit-linked and motor lines, while Bajaj Finserv Health revenue fell YoY and GI health loss ratio is rising.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bajaj Life retail with IndusInd Bank starts Q3 FY27, Bajaj AMC launched a PMS business and a real estate AIF first close, and Bajaj Finserv Direct is expected to break even in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Group investment funded from surplus capital
rows.why: Less than INR 2,000 crores of investment over 18 months against about INR 4,700 crores surplus capital plus dividends, with a possible one-time Ind AS surplus release as upside.

rows.label: Health cash burn falls and breakeven year after
rows.why: Bajaj Finserv Health cash consumption guided below INR 200 crores in FY27 and much lower next year, with breakeven targeted the year after.

rows.label: Ind AS transition for insurers from 1 April 2027
rows.why: Both insurers transition to Ind AS from 1 April 2027 and management expects no deferral, so this lands inside the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on lending, Life VNB (+40%) and AMC growth but cautious on the distribution consultation paper, health loss ratio and Life margin sustainability, and declined to quantify commission impact; analysts pressed on Life margins, non-par/annuity mix, and commission cuts.
